messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert PDC-4392 triggered for service=hosted-api · route=/v1/generate · severity=high · reason="sustained 5xx rate > 3% over 2m" · primary=devon · policy=prod-critical-escalation
 pagerduty: Alert auto-escalated to secondary (maria) after 2m no-ack
 devon: omg i'm on a different timezone, getting this now. just woke up, i'll check.
 maria: acked and taking it. looking at k8s and gateway logs now.
 erika: tagging in — Slack thread so we have visibility. customer-impact: some 3rd-party integrations are seeing errors, a handful of customers report high latency.
 maria: gateway logs show 502s from model-routing-service. traffic to the hosted-api pool 73% CPU on all nodes, lots of OOM kill traces for worker pods.
 sam: can we spin up extra nodes in the dedicated pool? autoscaler didn't kick hard enough.
 maria: trying a scale now, will also switch fallback model variant for heavy routes.
 maria: running:
 ```
 kubectl -n redwood scale deployment model-worker-hosted-api --replicas=12
 kubectl -n redwood get pods -l app=model-worker-hosted-api -o wide
 ```
 pagerduty: Escalation: no response from secondary within 5m -> manager notified (jessica)
 pagerduty: manager jessica paged via phone
 maria: scale command submitted, pending new nodes from cluster-autoscaler.
 devon: got it, standing by. I'm going to triage routing to see if a recent rollout caused this.
 erika: quick mitigation: can we flip route-level fallback to small-llm for non-critical tenants? that should cut tokens and reduce pressure.
 sam: yes, we have a runtime flag. pushing now:
 ```
 PATCH /runtime/routes/hosted-api/overrides
 { "fallback_model": "small-llm-v2", "apply_immediately": true }
 ```
 maria: fallback applied to 3 heavy routes. seeing CPU drop on model-worker-hosted-api pods.
 maria: new pods are still ImagePullBackOff on one node — looks like disk pressure. Ops team please advise.
 oncall-ops: disk pressure on node ip-10-2-7-43, evicting pods. spinning a replacement.
 alice: I've routed the affected customers to the secondary region (us-west-2) for reads; writes are still in primary.
 erika: status page draft:
 "We are investigating increased 5xx errors impacting text generation. Mitigations in progress (scaling, fallback models). Some customers may see degraded throughput."
 maria: confirmed a deployment from earlier today touched model-router config — reverting patch now.
 maria: reverting config:
 ```
 git revert --no-edit 7a2b3c4
 kubectl -n redwood rollout restart deploy/model-router
 ```
 maria: after rollback the error rate dropped from 3.9% -> 0.8% over 6 minutes.
 jessica: on call manager here — thanks for quick work. I’m awake and can escalate budget if we need hot nodes.
 devon: root cause looks like a bad routing flag that sent long-sequence requests to the small-quantized variant causing OOM cascades. rollback fixed the routing; scale + fallback bought us time.
 erika: customer communication ready, sending to SRE lead for review.
 sam: re: PagerDuty flow — primary missed page because phone DND was on. We should add a 3rd backup in the policy for overnight windows.
 jessica: agree. create a follow-up to adjust escalation policy and add a handler check for mobile DND.
 alice: created ticket INFRA-1127 for escalation policy change and a runbook note about phone-DND checks.
 oncall-ops: cluster-autoscaler brought nodes up, new pods stable, no further OOMs.
 maria: final verification: 5xx < 1% for 15m, p95 latency back to normal. closing alert.
 pagerduty: Alert PDC-4392 acknowledged by maria at 2024-06-21T12:14:22Z, resolved at 2024-06-21T12:40:51Z
 devon: thanks team. reminder to add a restraint check before routing changes in canary window.
 erika: adding action items:
 - INFRA-1127: add third oncall and DND detection to escalation policy (assigned: sam)
 - SRE-ops: add runbook step for immediate fallback to small-llm for heavy routes (assigned: maria)
 - QA: add test for routing-flag regressions in pre-prod (assigned: devon)
 :thumbsup: reactions across the thread
 maria: marking the thread as post-incident note in incident tracker, will start a short postmortem doc.
